**Finding the signed-in user on load**

`src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole app in `AuthLoader`. `AuthLoader` comes from `react-query-auth`, configured in `src/lib/auth.tsx` through `configureAuth(authConfig)`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios client. The session cookie goes along because the client sets `withCredentials`. While that request is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a full-screen spinner and doesn't render the app. When it resolves, the user is cached in TanStack Query and `useUser()` returns it everywhere. That includes `ProtectedRoute` in `auth.tsx`, which `src/app/router.tsx` wraps around the `/app` routes. If `user.data` is empty, `ProtectedRoute` redirects to the sign-in path with the current pathname as `redirectTo`, built by `paths.auth.login.getHref` in `src/config/paths`.

**When a request returns 401**

`src/lib/api-client.ts` defines the shared Axios instance `api`, and its response interceptor handles every error. It first shows an error toast with the server's message, or the Axios message if there is none, using `useNotifications` from `src/components/ui/notifications`. If the status is 401, it then does a full-page navigation with `window.location.href` to the sign-in URL, using `redirectTo`. The error is also re-rejected, so callers still see the failure.

This means a 401 on the initial `/auth/me` call gives a toast and a redirect to sign-in. A 401 on any later call, such as an expired session, does the same.

One quirk is in the interceptor. It builds `searchParams` from a fresh, empty `URLSearchParams()`, so `get('redirectTo')` always returns `null`. The redirect target is therefore always `window.location.pathname`. It is probably meant to read `window.location.search`. In practice the user still comes back to the page they were on, but any existing `redirectTo` on the current URL is ignored.
